small_guidance:
- The fused scale+mean tail is fine; runtime is dominated by `nn.ConvTranspose2d`. Tuning BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps further on the reduction kernel will not move fast_p — the conv accounts for nearly all 10.9 ms.
- If staying with this structure, at least fuse the multiplier into the conv bias path is not legal (changes nothing), so tuning here is exhausted.
- Consider channels_last memory format for the conv output so the subsequent reduction reads coalesced — but again, the conv itself is the bottleneck.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, IC tile, input-spatial tile)` computes the `input × weight` outer product over `(OC, kh, kw)` and atomically scatters into the strided output grid at `(n, oc, h*stride - pad + kh, w*stride - pad + kw)`. Handle `output_padding` in the index math.
- Fuse the `* multiplier` and the global mean directly into the scatter kernel's epilogue: instead of writing the full `(N, OC, H_out, W_out)` tensor, accumulate per-`(N, OC)` partial sums into a small buffer (atomic add on `out[N, OC]`) while still performing the full multiply-add count over the conv output grid. Then a trivial divide-by-`H_out*W_out*multiplier` finalizes — eliminates the giant intermediate tensor read/write.
- Alternative gather formulation: one program per `(N, OC)` loops over all `(ic, kh, kw, ih, iw)` accumulating `x[n,ic,ih,iw] * w[ic,oc,kh,kw]` for every contributing pair (i.e., full ConvT output positions enumerated implicitly), summing into a scalar then scaling. This materializes the full multiply-add count (N·OC·IC·kh·kw·H_in·W_in) without ever writing the H_out×W_out tensor. Use BLOCK_M over OC and a reduction loop over IC*kh*kw*H_in*W_in chunks; autotune (64/64, 128/64) with num_warps 4/8.
